evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Adds one restrained, non-blocking win accent using self-rescheduling after(), and insists on cancelling a pending after() when a new round starts.

pulse_winning_line schedules its own next tick via after() rather than blocking, so the event loop is never frozen. -- confirmed -- notebook 17-30 records ticks [0, 1] through a real mainloop, and the canonical implementation stores the job id and clears it.

cancel_pulse must call after_cancel before a reset, or a pending tick can fire on the new round's empty board. -- confirmed -- _pulse_job is non-None immediately after a win and None after cancel_pulse(); new_round() calls cancel_pulse() first, so the hazard is genuinely handled.

The effect is a single calm transition, not a flashing sequence: PULSE_BG, then after 400 ms the permanent WIN_BG. -- confirmed -- tick 0 paints #6EE7B7 and tick 1 paints #D1FAE5, one transition only. As found the effect was destroyed before completing because on_cell_leave called render() unconditionally (F-013, fixed against the project).

The three figures are three real frames of the effect. -- REFUTED as found -- win-pulse-step-1.png and win-pulse-final.png are byte-identical (also sharing x-win.png's hash). There are only two distinct frames. Fixed under F-020 by making the prose say so.
